artworks.title: Primary Doubt
artworks.description:
Coordinates set blind, then ruled out in pencil — 3D triangles and freemasonry symbolism drawn edge to edge — and the canvas turned upside down before any paint went on. Flat acrylic, no gradients, every edge painted to a line. Red, cobalt and yellow carry the grid; magenta, purple and orange break it. The third eye sits in the bottom right corner, worked in black and white, the one place the colour stops.

The subject is doubt: the thought that arrives at every step of making something, and at every step of living with bipolar. What the painting answers with is persistence — careful, correct colour coordination, and the determination to believe the work will be good.

hero.alt: A square canvas covered edge to edge in ruled, flat-painted triangles — red, cobalt, yellow, green, magenta, purple and orange — repeating outward as a kaleidoscope, with a black-and-white third eye in the bottom right corner.

insitu.alt: The same canvas hanging on a white studio wall, roughly as tall as the wall panel behind it, showing its scale.

details.alt: Close detail: a fan of cobalt and pale blue triangles opening into yellow and green.
Close detail: the tessellation repeating, with smaller triangles nested inside the larger ones.
Close detail: the third eye in the bottom right corner, worked in black and white — the only part of the canvas without colour.
